text:
incident-bot: Pager — canary v11 streaming latency anomaly in us-west-2. p95 ~ 600ms, p99 ~ 3.2s (SLO p99 800ms). Affected endpoints: /v1/stream, /chat/stream. Canary pool: canary-v11-usw2-shard2. Triggered at 2025-02-11T14:10:00Z. Paging oncall @Ryan_Oncall.

Ryan_Oncall: I'm on it, looking at dashboards now. tagging SREs and runtime.

Sara_SRE: seeing correlated increase in queue depth on shard2. streaming sessions show many "chunk timeout" events. raw sample: 
```
[14:11:03] stream_chunk_delay_ms=2500 conn_id=abc123 handler=kv-cache
[14:11:04] stream_chunk_delay_ms=3100 conn_id=def456 handler=encoder
[14:11:05] stream_chunk_timeout conn_id=ghi789
```

Mike_Eng: grabbing router logs — noticed sudden shift: 12% of canary traffic spiked to shard2 around 14:09. streak of small requests that shouldn't produce long sequences.

Ana_ML: v11 has a new attention kernel path which regresses for short sequences with streaming. Could cause stalls when kv-cache miss pattern hits. I can shadow profiling traces.

Sam_Platform: checking infra — GPU utilization on shard2 is normal (40-60%) but host event loop backpressure metrics are high. potential blocking in runtime I/O.

Ryan_Oncall: action plan: 1) throttle canary traffic to 2% (from 25%). 2) enable fallback routing to v10 for streaming routes. 3) increase client-side chunk timeout to 6s for customers with timeouts. 4) capture a heap/profile dump for Ana. Who can run the traffic throttle?

Mike_Eng: I can apply a temporary rate-limit in the routing policy. running: 
```
# routectl
routectl set-weight canary-v11 0.02 --region=us-west-2
```

Mike_Eng: pushed. canary weight now 2% in us-west-2. watch it.

Sara_SRE: enabling fallback for /v1/stream on the smart-router: 
```
fallback: v10
condition: streaming && region==us-west-2 && pool==canary-v11
```

Sara_SRE: fallback applied. starting to see p99 drop to ~1.1s within 30s. p95 stable ~450ms.

Ana_ML: requesting trace bundle from shard2 for 14:08–14:12 and a core profile. Posting S3 link in thread when ready. also recommend disabling the new attention kernel for v11 streaming path until we root cause.

Sam_Platform: kernel toggle available, applying to canary pool: 
```
runtime-toggle --pool canary-v11 --flag attention_kernel_new=false
```

Sam_Platform: toggle applied. observing additional improvements — p99 down to ~900ms. still above SLO but trending.

Jess_Product: any customer visible errors? should we notify customers or CS?

Liz_CS: I already have a support queue item from a mid-market customer complaining about intermittent streaming stalls starting ~14:10. I'll open a proactive ticket to impacted customers and include mitigation steps. No escalations yet.

Ryan_Oncall: good. next step is rollback vs gradual rollforward. Given the kernel regression signal and customer reports, prefer rollback for streaming-capable routes until ML confirms fix. Ana, can you sign off on safety of rollback?

Ana_ML: yes — rolling kernel toggle back to v10 behavior is safe. For full rollback we should revert canary traffic entirely (0%) and ensure no other pools are impacted. I'll validate model binary compatibility.

Mike_Eng: setting canary weight to 0 now. 
```
routectl set-weight canary-v11 0 --region=us-west-2
```

Mike_Eng: done. traffic shifted back to v10. p99 now ~610ms and stable.

Sara_SRE: confirming no residual stalls. Kv-cache miss rate back to normal. event-loop backpressure cleared on shard2.

Ryan_Oncall: marking incident as mitigated for live traffic. keeping thread open for RCA. tagging oncall handoff: @Ryan_Oncall -> @Sara_SRE for post-incident follow-up and RCA lead.

Jess_Product: prepping customer comms draft: short note, what happened, who was affected, mitigation, next steps. attaching to this thread for review.

Liz_CS: sending proactive messages to the two customers who reported stalls. included temporary workaround (increase client chunk timeout to 6s) and note that rollback completed.

Ana_ML: uploading trace bundle and profile: s3://redwood-traces/canary-v11/3377789000/tracebundle.tar.gz. initial look: attention_kernel_new introduces an extra blocking memcpy path for short sequences on certain GPU drivers. reproducer in lab created.

Mike_Eng: logs and routing histograms saved to: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/3377789000/. Will attach to RCA.

Sara_SRE: creating incident ticket and RCA stub. severity: S2 (partial customer impact, mitigation applied within 10 minutes). timeline notes: detection 14:10, throttle+fallback 14:12, kernel-toggle and weight->2% 14:13, fallback+toggle 14:14, full weight->0% 14:18, stable 14:21.

Ryan_Oncall: handing off to Sara for RCA and follow-up. leaving notes for next oncall: verify ML patch for kernel avoids blocking path, post-deploy canary with synthetic short-seq streaming load, and add alert that watches for sudden per-shard queue depth changes independent of GPU utilization.

Sara_SRE: acknowledged. will take primary owner. ETA for RCA draft: EOD 2025-02-12. If ML needs additional traces, ping me.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated (canary streaming latency). Pager closed. Incident ticket: INC-20250211-3377789000.

Ryan_Oncall: thanks team. leaving notes: no significant revenue impact identified. two customers saw degraded UX; CS engaged. Follow-up: add canary pre-deploy short-seq regression test to CI and add a canary rollback playbook snippet for streaming endpoints.

Liz_CS: will follow up with customers with post-mortem summary and recommended client-side settings if they want a safeguard.

Ana_ML: will open PR to revert new kernel path and add targeted perf tests. link in RCA when ready.

Sara_SRE: closing live thread; moving to RCA channel for deeper root cause.
